articles.title: Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars
articles.description: Japanese scientists will launch a spacecraft on Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars' moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Japan will launch the world's first mission to retrieve samples from one of Mars' moons in a historic space achievement. This groundbreaking mission represents a major leap in Mars exploration and sample return science.

articles.title: Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moon
articles.description: Japanese scientists are readying a mission to Mars' moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Japan is launching a historic round-trip mission to Mars' moons to retrieve samples that could reveal the origins of the solar system. This ambitious sample-return mission represents a major milestone in interplanetary exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
articles.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe. By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
articles.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded performance expectations by nearly 30% following precision engineering adjustments. This achievement promises even more groundbreaking discoveries in exoplanet and cosmology research.

articles.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
articles.description: Japan just launched an epic mission to Mars' moons that could make history as the first spacecraft to return to Earth from the Red Planet — and it plans to come back with samples onboard.
articles.summary: Japan has successfully launched the MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos, potentially making history as the first mission to return Martian moon samples to Earth. This groundbreaking mission marks a major achievement in planetary exploration.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his vision creating the IceCube observatory, a groundbreaking instrument for detecting high-energy neutrinos from the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA’s Simulated Mars Crew Marks One Year Inside Habitat
articles.description: The four crew members in NASA’s simulated Mars mission have spent the past year living and working in isolation in a confined habitat at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.
articles.summary: NASA's simulated Mars crew completes one year of isolated habitat living, providing crucial insights for future human Mars missions.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope makes its first discovery of a previously unknown comet, demonstrating its powerful detection capabilities.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration mission launches toward Mars's moons to unlock mysteries of the Martian system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter unravels the mystery of magnetic switchbacks, revealing how Earth's magnetic environment responds to solar wind interactions.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures spectacular imagery of energetic stellar jets from a nebula, revealing the violent birth processes of stars.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission begins its groundbreaking science operations to study how Earth's magnetosphere responds to solar wind.

articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures galaxies in unprecedented detail, revealing the intricate structures of a cosmic gravitational lens system. This Picture of the Month showcases JWST's remarkable ability to observe distant galactic structures.

articles.title: Webb Captures This Golden Galaxy Cluster in All it's Glory
articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features the brilliant golden galaxies belonging to the MACS J0454.1-0300 galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: JWST reveals a stunning golden galaxy cluster in exceptional detail as its Picture of the Month. The observation highlights the telescope's extraordinary capability to capture the brilliance of distant galactic structures.

articles.title: New Observations Show How Black Holes Stir Up Material Surrounding A Galaxy
articles.description: Supermassive black holes power tremendous jets that extend far beyond their galaxy. A new study finds how they can also warm material at the outer edge of a galaxy and reduce the rate of star production over time.
articles.summary: New research reveals how supermassive black holes stir and energize material throughout their host galaxies via powerful jets. The study advances our understanding of black hole physics and galactic evolution.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the source for the most energetic particles in the galaxy.
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the first-ever detection of a microblazar, a compact cosmic object distinct from larger blazars. This landmark discovery expands our understanding of high-energy phenomena in the universe.

articles.title: Cosmic 'hamburger' offers rare edge-on view of where giant planets may take shape
articles.description: Astronomers using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) were surprised to discover the earliest phases of giant planet formation between the dense layers of gas and dust in the "Gomez's Hamburger" system, referred to as GoHam.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: ALMA observations reveal an edge-on 'hamburger' structured disk showing the early stages of giant planet formation. This rare perspective provides new insights into planetary system genesis.

articles.title: Webb reveals metal-rich gas around Milky Way's central black hole
articles.description: The gas orbiting Sagittarius A (Sgr A*), the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy, is rich in metals, researchers at McGill University's Trottier Space Institute have found. The metal enrichment probably resulted from stars that exploded and released material into the black hole's surroundings over time, they said.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope reveals that gas orbiting Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center, is remarkably metal-rich. This discovery provides new understanding of black hole environments.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a ghostly green star unlike any known before
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered a surprising rainbow of dead stars, including the first known star that would appear genuinely green to human eyes. Researchers found that white dwarfs can glow in unexpected shades of pink, purple, yellow, and cyan because of unusual chemical interactions in their extremely dense atmospheres.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a rare green-hued dead star unlike any previously known, expanding our understanding of stellar diversity. This discovery reveals a surprising rainbow of stellar remnants in our galaxy.

articles.title: Two monster black holes could collide in just 100 years
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, with observations suggesting the pair completes an orbit every 121 days. Depending on their masses, these cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.
articles.summary: Astronomers have found compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a spectacular collision within approximately 100 years. This rare cosmic event offers unprecedented insights into black hole dynamics.

articles.title: NASA’s Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away
articles.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light-years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system, with three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds. The breakthrough gives scientists a powerful new tool for uncovering weather patterns on distant worlds and understanding the conditions that shape their atmospheres.
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has revealed surprising atmospheric dynamics on a mysterious world 20 light-years away. The discovery provides new insights into exoplanet weather patterns and atmospheric behavior.

articles.title: James Webb reveals a strange bulge in an alien planet's atmosphere
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered that a distant alien planet's atmosphere is surprisingly lopsided. Located 1,300 light-years away, the scorching gas giant WASP-17b experiences powerful winds that redistribute heat, causing one side of its atmosphere to bulge outward. A groundbreaking new mapping technique revealed these hidden distortions, confirming predictions about how extreme temperatures and winds shape alien worlds.
articles.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered an unexpected bulge in a distant exoplanet's atmosphere. This unusual atmospheric feature opens new avenues for understanding alien planetary systems.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a strange universal rule behind black hole eruptions
articles.description: Scientists have discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes appear to launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. The breakthrough could explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will happen.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a universal principle governing how black holes of vastly different sizes launch powerful jets. This breakthrough reveals fundamental physics applicable across the entire spectrum of black hole masses.

articles.title: Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon?
articles.description: Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a collision between Earth and a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia.
articles.summary: Scientists explore the giant-impact hypothesis, the leading theory explaining how a collision between Earth and a Mars-sized object formed our Moon.

articles.title: Astronomers Uncover More Intriguing Detail in an Ancient Supernova Remnant
articles.description: When a supernova exploded in 1181, Chinese and Japanese sky-watchers recorded it. They couldn't have known what the object was, and why it appeared for six months then disappeared. But in our modern times, we know it was a supernova, and we've even, most like…
articles.summary: Astronomers reveal new details about a supernova remnant from a 1181 explosion recorded by ancient Chinese and Japanese observers, deepening our understanding of stellar explosions.

articles.title: CHIME time, AI transparency in research, ‘Evolution’ on PBS, and faculty honors
articles.description: Yale researchers help prove the utility of an innovative radio telescope in understanding the expanding universe and offer thoughts on how to best use AI in science. Meanwhile, faculty members in physics and astronomy are honored for breakthroughs across an a…
articles.summary: Yale researchers demonstrate the innovative CHIME radio telescope's utility in understanding cosmic expansion and the universe's evolution.

articles.title: Physics Nobel highlights Antarctica’s role in exploring the cosmos
articles.description: For more than a century, scientists have treated Antarctica’s environments as windows into worlds beyond Earth.
articles.summary: Antarctica's unique environment serves as an ideal observatory for cosmic exploration, highlighted by the 2026 Nobel Prize recognition of Antarctic-based research.

articles.title: Bilder, Videos, Audio: NASA veröffentlicht gigantischen Datensatz zum Mond
articles.description:
Die Nasa veröffentlicht in dieser Woche einen riesigen Datensatz der Artemis-2-Mission. Warum die mehr als 800 Gigabyte an Mond-Daten so besonders sind.
weiterlesen auf t3n.de
articles.summary: NASA releases an extensive 800+ gigabyte dataset from the Artemis 2 mission, providing unprecedented lunar imagery and data for scientific research.

articles.title: Japan to launch first-ever mission to get samples from a Martian moon
articles.description: Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system.
articles.summary: Japan prepares to launch its first mission to collect samples from Phobos, a Martian moon, expected to reveal clues about the origin and evolution of Mars's moons.

articles.title: "Das wird ein knappes Rennen": Fabrik auf dem Mond soll nächste menschliche Zivilisationsstufe zünden
articles.description: Atomreaktoren und der Abbau des ultrakostbaren Isotops Helium-3 auf dem Mond sollen die Menschheit aufs nächste Level heben. Washington liefert sich mit Peking einen neuen Wettlauf ins All - getrieben von Tech-Milliardären wie Elon Musk, die Science Fiction m…
articles.summary: Visionary lunar factory concepts involving nuclear reactors and Helium-3 mining aim to propel humanity toward the next level of civilization through space-based resource utilization.

articles.title: NASA Improves Shock, Vibration Analysis
articles.description: Rockets vibrate, shake, and flex intensely as they climb into space, and spacecraft packed with delicate scientific instruments must survive those forces. Before any rocket leaves the ground, NASA engineers work to predict how those stresses will affect every part of a spacecraft. To do that, engineers in the Dynamic Environments Group with NASA’s Launch […]
articles.summary: NASA advances shock and vibration analysis technology to protect delicate scientific instruments during rocket launches and space travel.
